Someone who is teetotal never drinks alcohol at all — not occasionally, not socially, not even "just a sip." Zero. None. Ever.

The key idea is absoluteness. This is not a word about moderation. A person who drinks only on weekends is not teetotal. A person who drinks only wine, not beer, is not teetotal. A person who had their last drink ten years ago and hasn't touched alcohol since — that person is teetotal. The word only applies when the amount of alcohol consumed is a hard zero.

What it looks like in real life. If you go to a party and your friend orders a juice while everyone else has beer, and you ask them "don't you drink?" and they say "No, never have, never will" — your friend is teetotal. It is a word that describes a permanent, consistent, complete choice to stay away from alcohol.

What it does NOT tell you is why the person doesn't drink. Being teetotal says nothing about the reason. One person may be teetotal for religious reasons. Another because of a health condition. Another because alcohol ran through their family harmfully and they chose to break that pattern. Another simply because they don't enjoy the feeling. Another because they once had a problem with alcohol and decided to stop entirely. The word covers all of these people equally — it only speaks to the what (no alcohol), never the why.

• It does not mean the person judges or dislikes people who drink. A teetotal person can happily sit in a bar with friends and have no issue with others drinking around them.
  • It does not mean the person is "sober right now." Sober simply means not drunk at a given moment — even a heavy drinker is sober at 8 a.m. Teetotal is a lifestyle, not a momentary state.
  • It has nothing to do with food, caffeine, or any other substance. It is specifically, firmly about alcohol.
How it is used in sentences:

• "My uncle is teetotal, so don't bother offering him wine."
  • "She has been teetotal since her twenties."
  • "This is a teetotal household — we don't keep any alcohol here."
  • "He lives a teetotal life by choice, not for any medical reason."

Notice it can describe a person ("she is teetotal") or a lifestyle/choice/environment ("a teetotal household," "a teetotal life").

A small but useful note on related forms. The noun form of the word is teetotaler — meaning a person who is teetotal. ("He is a teetotaler.") The concept or practice is called teetotalism. But in everyday conversation, "teetotal" as an adjective is by far the most commonly used form.

One last thing to lock it in. Think of "teetotal" as the alcohol version of the word vegetarian, but even stricter. Just as a vegetarian eats no meat at all (not "very little meat"), a teetotal person drinks no alcohol at all. The moment there are exceptions, the word no longer applies.
